content: When transitioning a patient from a hospital setting to an ambulatory care setting, it is essential to perform a thorough medication reconciliation process as recommended by the American Diabetes Association (ADA). This involves reviewing all medications the patient is taking, including those prescribed at home and those initiated during the hospital stay. The purpose of this review is to identify and eliminate any duplicate therapies and to discontinue any medications that are no longer necessary. This meticulous process is critical in preventing adverse drug effects and ensuring optimal management of the patient’s condition by avoiding the use of unnecessary medications.
